# Contributing to FaceBlur

Thanks for your interest in FaceBlur! Bug reports, translations, design
feedback, code clean-ups and new features are all welcome. This page explains
how the project is organised and what a change needs before it can be merged.

## Ground rules

FaceBlur exists to blur faces **without the photos ever leaving the device**.
A few constraints follow from that and are not negotiable:

- **No network access.** The app declares no permissions at all, not even
  `INTERNET`. Changes that add one will not be merged.
- **No trackers, analytics, ads or crash reporters**, even "anonymous" ones.
- **Free software only.** Every dependency must be free software and available
  from a public repository, so that the app stays buildable by
  [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org). No Google Play Services, Firebase or
  proprietary SDKs.
- **No native code.** Face detection runs on a pure-Kotlin ONNX engine
  (`data/onnx`); there is no NDK, CMake or prebuilt inference library.
- **Reproducible release builds.** Two builds of the same commit must produce a
  byte-identical APK (see [Reproducible builds](#reproducible-builds)).

FaceBlur also deliberately stays small and simple. If you plan a large change
or a new feature, please open a
[feature request](https://github.com/gildas-le-drogoff/face-blur/issues/new/choose)
first so we can agree on the approach before you spend time on it.

## Reporting bugs

Use the [bug report form](https://github.com/gildas-le-drogoff/face-blur/issues/new/choose)
and include the app version, Android version and device. Face detection logs
are often useful:

```sh
adb logcat -d | grep FaceDetection
```

Please check the output for private data before pasting it, and **never attach
a photo of a real person** to a public issue.

**Security vulnerabilities** must not be reported as public issues: use a
[private security advisory](https://github.com/gildas-le-drogoff/face-blur/security/advisories/new)
instead.

## Translations

The app is available in English (default), French, German, Italian and
Spanish.

- App strings live in `app/src/main/res/values*/strings.xml`. English, in
  `values/`, is the reference and the fallback.
- Strings marked `translatable="false"` must not be translated.
- Keep the placeholders (`%1$d`, `%.2f`…) and the `plurals` quantities intact,
  and use the typographic characters of your language (`…`, `’`, non-breaking
  spaces before `:` in French, etc.).
- Store texts (title, short and full descriptions, changelogs) live in
  `fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/`. Only `en-US` and `fr-FR` exist so far;
  new locales are welcome.

**Adding a new language** also requires adding its code to `localeFilters` in
`app/build.gradle.kts`; otherwise the build strips it from the APK.

## Development setup

Requirements:

- JDK 21
- Android SDK with platform 37 (`compileSdk = 37`); `minSdk` is 29
- Android Studio is recommended but not required: everything goes through the
  Gradle wrapper

Build and install a debug version on a connected device or emulator:

```sh
./gradlew installDebug
```

Debug builds bundle a demo photo (`app/src/debug/assets/screenshot_demo.jpg`,
a face generated by StyleGAN2 — no real person) and offer an "Open the demo
photo" action, which is handy for testing without using your own pictures.

### Project layout

All the code lives in `app/src/main/java/fr/gildasledrogoff/faceblur/`:

| Package      | Contents                                                                                       |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `domain/`    | Pure logic with no Android dependency: data model, face selection, pixel effects, undo history |
| `data/`      | Image I/O, EXIF/XMP handling, settings, rendering, the YuNet detector and its decoder          |
| `data/onnx/` | The minimal pure-Kotlin ONNX runtime that executes the YuNet model                             |
| `ui/`        | Jetpack Compose screens and their ViewModels                                                   |

Unit tests mirror this layout under `app/src/test/`.

## Making a change

1. Fork the repository and create a branch from `main`.
2. Make your change, keeping **one concern per commit** with a clear commit
   message explaining *why*, not only *what*.
3. Add or update unit tests when you touch logic (see [Tests](#tests)).
4. Run the same checks as the CI:

   ```sh
   ./gradlew lint testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug
   ```

5. Open a pull request and fill in the checklist of the template.

### Code style

- Kotlin, following the official
  [Kotlin coding conventions](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/coding-conventions.html)
  and the style of the surrounding code (Android Studio's default formatter is
  fine).
- Code, comments and commit messages are written in English.
- Comments explain the *why* — constraints, trade-offs, non-obvious choices —
  rather than paraphrasing the code.
- User-visible text always goes in `strings.xml`, never hard-coded in Kotlin.
  When you add a string, add its translation for every supported language if
  you can; otherwise say so in the pull request so a translation can be added
  before the release.
- Icons are [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) vector
  drawables named `ic_*.xml` in `res/drawable/`.

### Tests

Unit tests run on the JVM (JUnit 4), without device or emulator:

```sh
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
```

Keep logic out of the Compose UI and Android framework classes where possible,
so that it can be tested this way: `domain/` must stay free of `android.*`
imports. `unitTests.isReturnDefaultValues` is enabled so that a stray
`android.*` call does not crash a test, but a test that depends on it is not
testing much.

### Licensing and REUSE

FaceBlur is licensed under the **AGPL-3.0-or-later**. By submitting a
contribution, you agree that it is distributed under that same licence.

The repository follows the [REUSE](https://reuse.software) specification,
checked by the CI:

- New source files start with the same SPDX header as the existing ones:

  ```kotlin
  // SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Gildas Le Drogoff and FaceBlur contributors
  //
  // SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
  ```

- Third-party material (images, icons, data…) under another licence needs an
  entry in [`REUSE.toml`](../REUSE.toml) and its licence text in
  [`LICENSES/`](../LICENSES), and must be compatible with the AGPL. It should
  also be credited in the in-app "Credits & licenses" screen and in the README.
- You can check compliance locally with the
  [`reuse`](https://github.com/fsfe/reuse-tool) tool:

  ```sh
  reuse lint
  ```

### Dependencies

Adding a dependency is a significant decision for an app of this size: it
grows the APK, widens the attack surface and must remain F-Droid-compatible.
Please justify any new dependency in the pull request. Versions are declared in
[`gradle/libs.versions.toml`](../gradle/libs.versions.toml); routine updates
are handled by Dependabot. GitHub Actions are pinned by commit SHA, with the
tag in a comment.

### Face detection model

The YuNet model (`app/src/main/assets/face_detection_yunet_2026may.onnx`) is
embedded as-is from the OpenCV Zoo and its checksum is verified by the CI.
Updating or replacing it requires updating, in the same commit:

- `face_detection_yunet_2026may.SOURCE.md` (pinned upstream URL, licence,
  SHA-256);
- the `.sha256` file;
- `REUSE.toml`, the in-app credits and the README if the file name or licence
  changes.

Any operator the new model needs must be implemented in the pure-Kotlin ONNX
engine; pulling in a native inference library is not an option.

### Reproducible builds

F-Droid rebuilds the app from source and checks that the result is identical to
the published APK. Do not introduce anything that makes the build depend on the
time, the machine or the build path: timestamps, generated build IDs,
`BuildConfig` fields filled at build time, stripping of native libraries, etc.

The *Reproducible build* workflow builds the release APK twice from two
different checkouts and compares them byte for byte. To check locally, build
twice from two clones and compare:

```sh
./gradlew clean assembleRelease
sha256sum app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk
```

Without `keystore.properties` the release APK is **unsigned**, which is
expected: F-Droid signs it with its own key.

## Screenshots, store texts and website

- Store screenshots (phone, 7" and 10" tablets, English and French) are
  generated from a running emulator — never take them by hand:

  ```sh
  ./generate-screenshots.sh --build
  ```

  The script requires `adb` and ImageMagick (and optionally `optipng`). It
  clears the app's data on the emulator.
- The store banner is generated by `tools/make-feature-graphic.sh` (ImageMagick 7
  and the Roboto fonts).
- The [project website](https://gildas-le-drogoff.github.io/face-blur/) is
  built by `tools/build-site.sh` from the fastlane metadata and published
  automatically when it changes on `main`: edit the fastlane texts, not the
  site.

## Releases (maintainer)

For reference, a release consists of:

1. Bumping `versionCode` and `versionName` in `app/build.gradle.kts`.
2. Adding `fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/changelogs/<versionCode>.txt` for
   every store locale.
3. Tagging the commit `v<versionName>`; F-Droid picks up new versions from
   these tags.

Pushing the tag runs the *Release* workflow, which publishes the signed
`faceblur-<versionName>.apk`, its checksums and build provenance attestations on
the [releases page](https://github.com/gildas-le-drogoff/face-blur/releases)
under the same tag. F-Droid verifies its own build against that APK, so a
published release is never replaced or deleted.

## Code of conduct

Be kind, patient and constructive. Everyone contributes on their free time, and
reviews are about the code, not the person.
